chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the boy who is breast-fed one feeding and two feedings, so he said: 'It does not make prohibition.' So I counted for him until I completed ten feedings, so he said: 'If they were separated, then no.'
ai.seo_question: How many breastfeedings are required to make marriage prohibited in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the threshold for establishing mahram status through radh, specifying that one or two feedings are insufficient and that the required feedings must be consolidated rather than scattered. It reflects the scholarly discussion on whether the number of feedings must be consecutive or can be cumulative, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) indicating that separated feedings do not suffice in this context. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining familial prohibitions and inheritance rights.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Fazzal, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the boy who is breast-fed the breast-feeding session, and the two breast-feeding sessions. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It does not make a Prohibition’. So I counted to him until I completed ten breast-feeding sessions. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was separated, so no’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a boy who is breastfed once and twice. He (the Imam) said, ‘It does not cause unlawfulness.’ I counted up to ten times breastfeeding. He (the Imam) said, ‘If they are on different times they do not cause unlawfulness.’”
